bib.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space

question: Can an LLM reason better by feeding its last hidden state back as the next input embedding (continuous thought) instead of generating language chain-of-thought tokens?
hypothesis: Language space is not always optimal for reasoning; reasoning in an unrestricted continuous latent space lets the model encode multiple alternative next steps (BFS-like) and gives a better accuracy/efficiency trade-off.
contributions: Coconut: feed last hidden state as next input embedding, trained with a multi-stage curriculum from language CoT
ProsQA, a new logical reasoning dataset requiring planning over a DAG
Analysis showing continuous thoughts encode multiple next steps, resembling BFS tree search

method.summary: Coconut switches between language mode and latent mode delimited by <bot>/<eot>; in latent mode the previous last hidden state replaces the input embedding. Trained with a multi-stage curriculum that replaces the first k CoT steps with k*c continuous thoughts, loss masked on question and thoughts. Evaluated with GPT-2 on GSM8k, ProntoQA, ProsQA, plus Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3-8B on GSM8k.

datasets.name: GSM8k
datasets.source: Cobbe et al. 2021; training uses synthetic dataset generated by Deng et al. (2023)

datasets.name: ProsQA
datasets.source: new, constructed by the authors (Appendix A.2, Algorithm 1); DAG avg 23.0 nodes, 36.0 edges, shortest path 3.8, 1.6 shortest paths
datasets.preprocessing: binary question 'Is [Entity] a [Concept A] or [Concept B]?', A/B randomly permuted

training.objective: negative log-likelihood (cross-entropy) on tokens after the continuous thoughts; loss masked on questions and latent thoughts; n+1 sequential forward passes for n latent thoughts
training.epochs: ProsQA: 5 per stage, 6 stages, then stay in last stage until 50 epochs. GSM8k (GPT-2): 6 epochs initial stage, 3 per later stage, 50 total. ProntoQA: 5 per stage, 50 total. Llama: 3 epochs stage 0 then 1 per later stage

other.curriculum: stage k replaces first k reasoning steps with k*c continuous thoughts; stage 0 is regular CoT; optimizer state reset at each stage switch
other.c: GSM8k c=2 with 3 stages plus an extra stage with all language removed (3*c thoughts); ProntoQA/ProsQA c=1 with 6 stages; Llama c=1
other.c=3: slight drop and higher variance, loss spike at stage transition
other.lr_batch_note: lr and batch size given only in the ProsQA setup; assumed shared, not stated for others

inference.prompting: <bot> inserted after question; latent thoughts padded to constant length matching final training stage; a binary classifier for <eot> worked comparably

parameters.k: number of continuous thoughts forced at inference on ProsQA, k in 0..6

results.quote: while “lempus” initially has the highest value (0.33) at the first reasoning step (Figure 5, left), the model subsequently assigns the highest value (0.87) to “rorpus,” a child of “grimpus,”

limits: Coconut does not surpass CoT on GSM8k (34.1 vs 42.9)
Training needs language CoT supervision; without curriculum it is no better than no-CoT
Gains shrink on larger pretrained models (Llama 3-8B 43.6 vs 42.2); authors suggest latent pretraining is needed
Training is sequential (n+1 forward passes), hard to parallelise
On ProntoQA/ProsQA, iCoT, w/o thought and pause-as-thought match Coconut, so compute may not be the bottleneck there
BFS claim rests on probing of one case study plus aggregate plots
